title: fix(swf): SWF_BLEND_MODE byte table is off-by-one — all non-normal blend modes render wrong
description:
In packages/swf/src/filters.ts, the SWF_BLEND_MODE lookup table is off by one:

  SWF_BLEND_MODE = { normal:0, layer:1, multiply:2, screen:3, ... overlay:12, hardlight:13 }

Ruffle's BlendMode enum (ruffle/swf/src/types.rs) is:
  Normal=0, Layer=2, Multiply=3, Screen=4, ... Overlay=13, HardLight=14

Ruffle's from_u8() maps byte 1→Normal and byte n→n for all other values.

The FLA importer (flash8-import.ts BLEND_MODE_MAP) correctly maps byte 2→layer, byte 3→multiply, etc.

The SWF encoder is wrong: when a model has blendMode='layer', we emit byte 1, which Ruffle treats as Normal. When we emit 'multiply', we emit byte 2, which Ruffle treats as Layer. Every non-normal blend mode is shifted by one and renders as the wrong effect.

The existing tests in blendmode.test.ts also encode wrong expected values (expecting multiply=2, overlay=12) and must be updated alongside the fix.

## Root Cause
SWF_BLEND_MODE was built with 0-based indexing starting from normal=0, but the SWF spec (and Ruffle) use:
  - 0 or 1 = Normal
  - 2 = Layer
  - 3 = Multiply
  - 4 = Screen
  - 5 = Lighten
  - 6 = Darken
  - 7 = Difference
  - 8 = Add
  - 9 = Subtract
  - 10 = Invert
  - 11 = Alpha
  - 12 = Erase
  - 13 = Overlay
  - 14 = HardLight

## Fix
Update SWF_BLEND_MODE in packages/swf/src/filters.ts:
  { normal:1, layer:2, multiply:3, screen:4, lighten:5, darken:6, difference:7,
    add:8, subtract:9, invert:10, alpha:11, erase:12, overlay:13, hardlight:14 }

Also update the blendmode.test.ts expected values (multiply: 2→3, overlay: 12→13).

The 'normal' guard in compile.ts/sprite.ts (blendMode !== 'normal') means normal objects never reach encodePlaceObject3WithBlendMode, so changing normal from 0→1 has no practical effect but aligns with spec.

## Acceptance
- compileDocument with blendMode='multiply' emits PlaceObject3 with blend byte 3 (not 2)
- compileDocument with blendMode='overlay' emits PlaceObject3 with blend byte 13 (not 12)
- All blendmode.test.ts tests pass with corrected values
- A Ruffle E2E oracle confirms 'multiply' renders differently from 'normal' and 'layer'
